title: Contact Center routing
blurb: Entry points, queues, teams, and the difference between a Webex Calling call queue and a contact center queue.

lessons.title: Three contact centers
lessons.summary: Webex Contact Center, Webex Contact Center Enterprise, and the on-premises UCCX and UCCE products are not one queue with three names.
objectives: Separate cloud Webex Contact Center from Enterprise
Point UCCX and UCCE at their own Cisco pages
Refuse a script import that does not exist

lessons.title: Queues, LAA, and BAA
lessons.summary: Longest available and best available are the routing strategies the routing article describes. This lab does not invent a third name or a RONA timer.
objectives: Separate this from Calling call-queue algorithms

diagram.caption: The queue holds the contact. The strategy picks the agent.

flow.title: Choose a strategy you can cite

steps.label: Queue Contact
steps.detail: The activity places the contact in a contact center queue. It is not the Calling call queue.

steps.label: Pick LAA or BAA
steps.detail: The routing article is the source for longest available and best available. Use its words in your design notes.
steps.inspect: Open the live page when you configure

steps.label: Do not invent RONA
steps.detail: This lab does not publish a ring-no-answer timer. If the article you are implementing states one, cite that sentence.

steps.label: Different algorithms
steps.detail: Circular, Top Down, Longest Idle, Weighted, and Simultaneous belong to the Webex Calling call queue article, with the caps published there.
steps.inspect: Do not paste those caps onto WxCC

paragraphs: Webex Calling call queues publish priority-based patterns and agent caps. Contact center routing publishes LAA and BAA.
Using the Calling word Circular in a contact center design review is how the wrong article gets implemented.

cite.label: Routing and queueing in Webex Contact Center

paragraphs: No RONA seconds, no undocumented overflow percentages, no skill-score formula that is not on the page you cite.
Queue To Agent is a different activity: it targets an agent id or email. That is preference, not LAA.

lessons.title: Resource collections
lessons.summary: A user profile can hold up to five resource collections. Collections decide which queues, flows, and analyzer data a person can see.

diagram.caption: Five collections on the profile. The default collection catches what they create.

flow.title: Why an admin sees two queues and not twenty

steps.label: Group the resources
steps.detail: The access article allows up to five resource collections on a user profile. That fences Control Hub, Flow Designer, Analyzer, and Desktop.

steps.label: Pick one
steps.detail: If they can create a resource but cannot choose a collection, it is added to the default so they do not lose it.

steps.label: Watch 15 and 350
steps.detail: A collection cannot be added to a user profile if it is already on 15 other profiles. A collection can hold up to 350 selected resources. An organization can have up to 1,000 collections.

steps.label: Same fence
steps.detail: Teams in the collection are the teams they see. Analyzer data follows the same queues.

paragraphs: All resources is different from a list of collections. Someone with all resources and edit access can create collections. Someone limited to selected collections cannot create new ones even with edit access.
Deleting a resource requires a profile with All resources. A delegated admin who only removes it from the collection then loses access to it.

cite.label: Manage access in Webex Contact Center

paragraphs: If you grant view or edit on a type such as skill profiles but add none to the collection, the navigation entry appears and the list is empty. The article says you are warned and not blocked.
Fix the collection. Do not debug Flow Designer for an empty list that access control explains.

cite.label: Manage access in Webex Contact Center
